prestigious

press-TIJ-us — stress the TIJ; a prestigious prize always gets good press. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Prestigious is admired and respected as one of the very best of its kind.

She was accepted into a prestigious university known around the world.

Example

Scientists spend their whole careers dreaming of one particularly prestigious medal. Winning it instantly makes international headlines, and past recipients include the most celebrated researchers in history. Universities proudly list even a single winner on their websites for decades.

The medal is admired as the very best honor its field can offer. Unlike 'popular,' which means widely liked, prestigious means carrying high status and earning deep respect.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

acclaimed: Acclaimed means publicly praised, especially by critics, for a particular achievement or work. Prestigious describes standing rather than applause: a prestigious institution or award carries lasting high status that rubs off on anyone connected to it. Acclaim is the praise you receive; prestige is the rank you hold.

distinguished: Distinguished usually describes a person who has earned honor through long, excellent work — a distinguished judge or professor. Prestigious more often describes the institution, award, or position itself, whose reputation confers status on those who hold it. A distinguished scientist may spend her career at a prestigious university.

respected: Respected means held in high regard — people trust and admire it. Prestigious raises the bar: a prestigious school is not just respected but ranked among the very best of its kind, so its name alone carries weight. Every prestigious school is respected; most respected schools are not prestigious.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

disreputable: having a bad reputation

humble: ordinary and low in status

Where it sits · how great the fame has grown — reputable → prestigious → legendary

reputable vs. prestigious: Reputable is weaker than prestigious — a reputable school is simply trustworthy and decent, while a prestigious one commands top-tier admiration.

legendary vs. prestigious: Legendary is stronger than prestigious: a legendary award is so admired that its fame has become the stuff of stories.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — prestig

Root — prestig: dazzling illusion, conjurer's trick (from Latin praestigiae, a juggler's tricks)

Suffix — -ious

Suffix — -ious: full of (Latin -osus)

Put it together

Put it together: Prestig ('dazzling illusion, conjurer's trick' — from Latin praestigiae, a juggler's dazzling tricks) + -ious ('full of'): prestigious originally meant 'full of illusion.' Over time the 'dazzle' shifted from trickery to reputation — something so admired it dazzles us.

Use the root in a new word: prestige

Use the root in a new word: prestige: Winning the state championship brought great prestige to the small school.
